pin_row_note: pin_row_y is the HEADPIN base row derived in the same frame from the edge lines: the row where lane width = 7-column pin spread (61.4 px at f470/f489/f490 = 36 in) x 41.5/36 x 1.043 (headpin 31 in in front of the back row). Read through the reflections the pin bases look ~10-20 px lower; that is the deck reflection, not the base. Canary: in f480 the edge lines at y=600 sit 4.7 px (= 2.75 in at 1.71 px/in) outside the 7- and 10-pin columns, which is where the physical deck edge is.
observed_pin_contact_note: Cut pin_hit_frame 480 is ~10 frames early. Frames 481-489: the ball is a dark purple blob drawn OVER standing, undisturbed pins (in front of the rack, ~12 px wide at f484, not glimpsed through 2-4 px gaps) moving left; at f489-491 its contact row reaches the headpin row (lane width at the ball row 71-72 px = pin-ruler width); first pin lean f492-494; pins fly f496. Contact 490 +-2. 192142 crops: seq_481_489.jpg, seq_490_504.jpg, gcgrid_482_488.jpg, gcgrid_490_494.jpg, gcgrid_489_491.jpg.

entry.note: Real entry at the observed contact (f490 +-2). The ball moves ~1.5-2 boards per frame here, so the +-1 frame reads span 19-23 and the uncertainty is mostly timing. Pin ruler: 7 columns 397/407.6/417.6/427.6-428/438/448/458.4 px at f489-490 (10.23 px = 6 in = 5.49 board units), headpin column 428 (f489) / 427.6 (f490), ball x 430 / 424.5. Ball ruler: board = 20 - (x_ball - x_headpin) x 7.8 / (2r), r 7.5.

entry_at_cut_pin_hit.note: reads at the cut pin_hit_frame-1/0/+1 as the task named them; the ball is still short of the pins here, so this is NOT the entry board

method: Ball centre and radius read by eye on 3x/5x gridded crops of the SOURCE frames (cv2 seek canary: MAD 1.8 at offset 0 vs 5-12 at +-1), confirmed against a purple/dark blob circle drawn on an overlay; lane edges are the wood-to-gutter-lip step found per row on 5-8 rows of THE SAME FRAME that are clear of the ball and of the pin reflections, fitted as a straight line (residual <=1.8 px) and evaluated at the ball row y (board) and at y+r (board_contact). board = 1 + 38*(x - right_x)/(left_x - right_x); pin ruler uses the 7 pin columns (6 in apart = 5.49 units of lane/38, headpin = 20); ball ruler uses 8.5 in = 7.8 units anchored on the headpin column.
limits: Cut pin_hit_frame 480 is ~10 frames before contact (observed ~490), so the path is extended to f490 and entry.board is read at f490, not 480; the cut-frame reads are kept in entry_at_cut_pin_hit. Near the pins the edge lines are extrapolated 30-76 px from rows in front of the deck; their slopes vary 0.33-0.42 frame to frame, worth ~3-5 px of width, which is ~0.3 board near the lane centre but several feet of depth, so pin_row_frame is +-2 frames. Ball x at f482/f486 is +-3 px (smeared over pins), ~1.5 boards. The ball moves 1.5-2 boards per frame in the last 6 frames, so a +-2 frame contact error is +-3-4 boards of entry. The pin ruler is biased low by 1.5-2 boards whenever the ball is in front of the pins (f479/f480 cut reads 9.2 vs edges 10.9-11.2), so only the f489/f490 pin-ruler reads count for entry. Release frame (415) unchanged from loop 1.

pin_row.frame_contact_row_note: ball bottom (y+r) reaches the headpin base row f489-491 (existing observed_pin_contact_note, lane width at the ball row = pin-ruler width); among the pins the ball's y is +-3 px, so +-2 frames
pin_row.note: Verified: ball centre y 601 at f488 vs head base 596.7 (not yet), 598.1 at f489 vs ~597.9 (tie within 0.2 px), 595 at f490 vs 599 (reached). Kept 490. Refit = my own edge fit on rows 631-671 at f490 (rms 0.34/0.66 px).
pin_row.est_60ft_note: contact_frame - k, k=0 = rack row of the first pin within 6.1 units of the ball's board (about 1 frame per row); first visible pin motion lags the touch, so this is an upper bound

contact_note: First visible pin lean f493-494 on zoom_489_500_420_595.jpg (pins left of the ball at x 390-410); aligned pin-region change rises 9.4 (f490) -> 12.6 (f491) -> 15.5 (f493) -> 18.6 (f494), but the ball is inside that window so the series only brackets it. Pins fly f495-496. +-1.

exit.deflection: entered left of the headpin (board ~22, Brooklyn side), deflected left through the 2-4-7 side at 2-3 boards per frame and left the deck at its left edge by the 7-pin

exit_method: Ball positions read by eye on 5x and 8x camera-followed gridded crops (gc_<f>_z.jpg, zoom_489_500_420_595.jpg, zoom_493_501_395_592.jpg) and cross-checked against moving purple HSV components (blob.py); lane edges are the wood-to-gutter Sobel step on rows 629-671 in front of the deck in the same frame, straight-line fit (rms <= 0.66 px), evaluated at the ball row. Pin ruler: the 7 pin columns of f490 (397..458.4 px, headpin 427.8, 10.23 px = 6 in = 5.494 units) shifted by the measured camera dx (-7.0 px) to f497; back row 7/8/9/10 = 36.48/25.49/14.51/3.52 computed from 12-in spacing.
exit_limits: Edge lines are extrapolated 32-74 px from the fitted rows to the ball row. From f496 the ball merges with a static purple-tinged dark patch left of the deck (present at x 381-386 from f486, before the ball arrives; merged area 324-331 at f496-498 vs 146 at f495), so f497 is the last frame the ball is a separate disc; a faint blob at x 384-388 to f507 is that static patch and was not counted. Ball x at f496-497 is +-3 px under falling pins (~1.5 boards); the deck spans only ~5 px of rows (head 599, back 594 at f490), so depth on the deck is not resolved.
